thread:
maria: Heads-up — hit a weird case where generator stream doesn't cancel when ctx.Done fires in the onboarding sample. Repro steps below.

raj: hmm can you paste a minimal repro? I remember something similar with auth refresh midstream.

maria: repro: call Generate(ctx) then cancel ctx after first token. stream goroutine stays around ~30s. logs: 
```
2026-03-20T12:04:01Z stream started
2026-03-20T12:04:01Z token received
2026-03-20T12:04:31Z stream goroutine exit
```

sam: ouch. was this using the default client or the sampleapp shim? did you enable auth retry?

maria: default client, no explicit auth retry. behavior looks like the SDK waits for in-flight retry/backoff timer before shutting down; ctx cancel doesn't short-circuit the backoff.

emily: probable root cause: our auth refresh/backoff path uses time.After and doesn't select on ctx.Done(), so cancel isn't respected.

raj: from an API/ergonomics POV we should return a Stream object (io.ReadCloser-style or grpc-like Recv()) rather than raw channels. current Generate(ctx, req) -> (<-chan Token, <-chan error, error) forces callers to do a lot of coordination.

maria: yeah current signature in sampleapp: `func Generate(ctx context.Context, req *GenRequest) (<-chan Token, <-chan error, error)` — it's noisy and easy to misuse.

devex-bot: FYI — we've linked this to GH issue #1204 (generator ergonomics + ctx cancellation).

sam: concrete proposal: change to an explicit stream interface so callers can `defer stream.Close()` and Recv will return ctx-aware errors. e.g.:
```
type GenerationStream interface {
  Recv() (Token, error) // like grpc/httputil readers
  Close() error          // ensure transport + server cancel
}
func Generate(ctx context.Context, req *GenRequest) (GenerationStream, error)
```
That gives a clear lifecycle and we can ensure Close cancels internal goroutines.

emily: also pls make the auth retry cancellable: use `select { case <-time.After(backoff): case <-ctx.Done(): }` in our retry loop so we don't block shutdown.

maria: agreed. onboarding friction is real — the sample app currently demonstrates the channel pattern and people copy it. We should update sample and README with the new pattern and a tiny example using `context.WithCancel` + `defer stream.Close()`.

raj: non-blocking work: add a short snippet under `go-sdk/onboarding/` and a deprecation note for the old channel API. tests should assert no leaked goroutines during stream cancel in CI.

maria: I'll open a PR that does two things: (1) make backoff cancellable, (2) introduce GenerationStream interface + adapter for old API. want reviews from @sam and @emily. cc @raj for testing plan.

sam: happy to review, please include a small unit test that simulates auth refresh taking long and ensure ctx cancel returns quickly.

emily: can review too. also add a tiny doc blurb about auth retry semantics in the Go README.

maria: thanks all — filing PR/issue now. I'll also add a tiny e2e sample in the sampleapp to demonstrate `context.WithCancel` usage and best-practice pattern.

sam: 👍

emily: 👍

maria: filing issue for metrics as well — would be nice to detect leaked goroutines in CI when streams are canceled.
